summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old woman was admitted for elective right total knee arthroplasty due to severe osteoarthritis. She has a complex medical history including chronic pancreatitis, hypertension, depression, PTSD, restless legs syndrome, asthma, venous insufficiency, and a history of MRSA infections and DVT. The surgery was performed successfully on the day of admission. Postoperatively, she received IV antibiotics and lovenox for prophylaxis, was transitioned from PCA to oral pain control, and began physical therapy with weight-bearing as tolerated and CPM machine use. She required one unit of blood on postoperative day one due to anemia from a hematocrit of 27. Her recovery was uncomplicated, with stable vital signs, adequate pain control, and a clean, healing incision. She was discharged home with home health services, instructions for wound care, anticoagulation with lovenox followed by aspirin, and a follow-up appointment in four weeks.
